text:
alex: Heads-up — found a new class of warnings from rollout telemetry when a client pins an ephemeral / short-lived model variant. They show up as 'pin_incompatibility' in the logs and are noisy. Anyone else seen this?

maria: yep saw it in last night's canary. pretty noisy, mostly harmless but annoying for oncall.

chris: how are the warnings generated? are they brokering schema mismatch between pin metadata and the runtime's expectations?

alex: looks like this: the client sets pin.metadata.features = ["kv_cache"] but the runtime has reconciled quantization_profile = "q4_0" and we evaluate compatibility against a stricter contract. telemetry currently emits a top-level warning with the full diff.

kaitlin: can you paste the log snippet?

alex: sure:

```
WARN rollout.telemetry pin_incompatibility tenant=acme variant_id=xyz123 mismatch={"metadata.features": ["kv_cache"] -> null, "quantization_profile": "q4_0" -> "q8_0"}
```

maria: so the client pinned expecting kv_cache support but the serving variant doesn't advertise it. We should avoid surfacing raw diffs to users and fold these into a clearer contract: e.g., 'requested feature X not available on served variant Y'.

chris: +1. Two parts to consider: (1) what counts as an incompatibility vs a soft-degradation (2) how to represent it in the pin schema so clients can programmatically handle it.

kaitlin: tradeoffs: stricter schema means fewer surprises but more breakages on rollout; softer (warnings only) keeps apps online but users might silently degrade. For ephemeral pins (TTL < 1h) leaning toward warnings only.

alex: suggestion: add a 'compatibility_level' enum to pin metadata: REQUIRED | PREFERRED | BEST_EFFORT. Default = PREFERRED for backwards compat. REQUIRED would cause a hard reject at control plane.

maria: love that. also we should change telemetry shape from a freeform diff to a typed event: {result: REJECTED|WARN|OK, reason: string, fields: ["quantization_profile"]}. That way alerting and UIs can group by reason.

chris: implementation note: the runtime currently computes compatibility by walking two dicts and producing a diff. Converting to typed events is easy-ish but we must be careful about semantics for nested fields and arrays. e.g., metadata.features is an array; membership checks vs equality matters.

kaitlin: for array fields we probably want membership semantics by default (requested subset -> ok if served superset), equality only for things like architecture or tokenizer. We should document per-field semantics in the pin schema.

alex: agree. action items: (1) add compatibility_level to pin schema + docs (2) change telemetry contract to typed events (WARN/REJECT/OK) and include canonical reason codes (FEATURE_MISSING, INCOMPATIBLE_QUANT, VERSION_MISMATCH) (3) decide per-field semantics and include 'matching_strategy' per field defaulting to SUBSET or EQUAL.

maria: +1. Can we also make the telemetry emit a single top-level summary per pin attempt so oncall isn't flooded? e.g., one event per pin attempt with aggregated field reasons.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: rollout-service (canary) - config-change compat-telemetry-schema. estimated deploy: 02:10 UTC.

chris: good call. For backward compat, we should support the old diff payload for one release and convert consumers to the typed event. We'll add a feature flag to toggle the new format.

kaitlin: timeline: propose RFC doc this week, ship change in two sprints with feature flag. I'll draft the RFC and include sample event shapes + per-field match rules.

alex: thanks. one more UX ask — in Console, pin UI should show a 'compatibility preview' before you confirm pin: list which requested fields might be downgraded and suggested alternatives. That will reduce support tickets.

maria: agree. I'll take the console piece if someone posts the sample API response shape.

alex: ok i'll add the sample shape to the RFC draft. tagging @kaitlin for RFC ownership. :thumbsup:
